meta.title_passenger: P2L User — Discover what you need near you
meta.title_driver: P2L Operator — Operate where the demand is
meta.title_fleet: P2L Business — Turn your location into a sales channel
meta.description: P2L is a location-based platform connecting supply and demand for mobility, goods, services, and deliveries through geographic channels, geofences, and broadcast.

passenger.eyebrow: 👤 User · Supply and demand near you
passenger.title: Discover what you need near you
passenger.lead: Move, discover businesses, find services, and request products based on your location. P2L connects your demand with nearby supply.

driver.eyebrow: ⚙️ Operator · Driver, courier, or field worker
driver.title: Operate where the demand is
driver.lead: Receive requests, fulfill services, and discover opportunities as you move through your area. Operators also take part in P2L’s supply-and-demand network.

fleet.title: Turn your location into a sales channel
fleet.lead: Activate the broadcast of your geographic channel (geofence) and let people and operators discover your business, products, and services when they are nearby. Your company. Your zone. Your channel.

passenger.benefits_title: P2L connects your demand with nearby supply
passenger.benefits_lead: Supply and demand connected by location: mobility, goods and services, and deliveries on one geographic platform.
passenger.b1_text: Request a ride and find available operators near you. Map, chat, and live tracking.
passenger.b2_text: Find restaurants, shops, properties, and services around your location — even if you have not requested a ride.
passenger.b3_text: Request products and services from businesses that operate in your area, through the company’s geographic channel broadcast.
passenger.services_title: Choose how you want to take part in P2L
passenger.services_lead: One platform. Three ways in: user, operator, or business. Everything connected by location.
passenger.s1_text: Request a ride, find nearby businesses, order deliveries, and subscribe to geographic channel broadcast.
passenger.s2_text: Driver, courier, or field operator: fulfill nearby services and also discover local supply.
passenger.s3_title: Publish your offer and activate your channel
passenger.s3_text: Restaurant, shop, realtor, hotel, fleet, or store: your business has a channel inside the map.
passenger.s4_text: Request a ride, set origin and destination, and connect with available operators near you.
passenger.s5_text: Discover properties, restaurants, shops, and professional services around your location.
passenger.s6_text: Enter the broadcast (geofence), discover a business, subscribe to its channel, and get alerts when you return.
passenger.how_lead: Sign in with Google and start discovering nearby supply.
passenger.step1_text: Access with Google from the web or your device. No long forms.
passenger.step2_text: Move around, find nearby businesses, or request a ride or a delivery in your area.
passenger.step3_text: Subscribe to the geographic channel broadcast, chat with the business, and get alerts when you return.
passenger.highlight_title: Your location connects supply with demand
passenger.highlight_text: Broadcast is the business geofence: Airbnb with a fixed point, delivery in an operating radius, or the venue you just walked into. Subscribe once to the channel; when you return, the app notifies you and opens chat with the business. An Uber-like experience to move, Airbnb-like to discover local supply, and Rappi-like to request deliveries.
passenger.lost_text: If you used mobility, you can contact the operator from the app or report an issue to get help.
passenger.cta_text: Receive requests, fulfill services, and discover opportunities in your area. You can also register your business and activate your geographic channel broadcast.

driver.benefits_title: Connect your work with demand in your area
driver.benefits_lead: Operators do more than fulfill services. They also take part in P2L’s supply-and-demand network as they move.
driver.b1_text: Receive services and requests from users who are nearby: rides, deliveries, or field work.
driver.b2_text: Manage statuses, routes, requests, and services from your device, whenever you choose to go online.
driver.b3_text: Coordinate directly with users and businesses. The same conversation in the app and on the dashboard.
driver.services_lead: Driver, courier, operator, or service staff: everything you need to operate on the geographic platform.
driver.s1_text: Go online to receive nearby requests and pause when you are not available.
driver.s2_text: Review origin, destination, and estimated value before accepting a service.
driver.s3_text: Manage status: on the way, at the meeting point, and completed.
driver.s4_text: See the route and the user’s location throughout the service.
driver.s5_text: Review completed services and recent activity for the day.
driver.s6_text: As you move through an area you can also discover nearby businesses, services, properties, and offers, subscribe to the channel broadcast, and chat.
driver.how_lead: Register in the panel, join a company or create yours, and open the app.
driver.step1_text: Enter the company panel and create or join an organization.
driver.step2_text: The admin adds you as an operator. You open the app and sign in.
driver.step3_text: Go online, accept nearby services, and discover supply in your area.
driver.highlight_title: Operators also take part in the network
driver.highlight_text: You do more than fulfill services. Enter the radius of a shop, a property, or a delivery zone, subscribe to the channel broadcast, and the business can reconnect when you return.
driver.cta_text: Connect your work with demand in your area and discover nearby businesses as you move. You can also register your own company.

fleet.benefits_title: Your company. Your zone. Your channel.
fleet.benefits_lead: P2L lets any business activate a location-based commercial presence: restaurant, shop, realtor, hotel, delivery, transport, or fleet. Your business has a channel inside the map.
fleet.a1_text: Activate a broadcast (geofence) and let nearby people discover your business. Register name, phone, and responsible person.
fleet.a2_text: Offer products, services, properties, deliveries, and more. Invite your operations team and control seats according to your plan.
fleet.a3_text: Choose Starter, Growth, Business, or Enterprise. Pay with ePayco. The passenger pays the operator directly; P2L is covered by the plan and the prepaid balance.
fleet.a4_text: Users and operators can discover your broadcast, subscribe to the channel, and chat with you when they are nearby.
fleet.a5_text: Manage your company, team, services, fleet, and wallet from the dashboard.
fleet.a6_text: When you create the company, the chosen plan quotas apply. Then you renew with ePayco (30 days).
fleet.plans_lead: Three company types (mobility, deliveries, bookings). Same dashboard structure: seats, prepaid wallet, and suggested company participation. 5-day trial; paid plans renew with ePayco.
fleet.how_title: How you activate your geographic channel broadcast
fleet.how_lead: Business → broadcast (geofence) → offer → nearby people and operators discover the channel → they subscribe → chat → alerts when they return.
fleet.step1_text: Enter the dashboard, register your restaurant, shop, property, hotel, store, delivery, or fleet, and choose the trial plan.
fleet.step2_text: Set your broadcast (geofence), publish your offer, and invite operators. Control seats according to the contracted plan.
fleet.step3_text: Monitor wallet, services, and subscribers. When the trial ends, pay with ePayco to renew 30 days.
fleet.cta_text: Your business has a channel inside the map. Users and operators discover your products, services, properties, or deliveries when they are nearby.

geo.slogan: Your location connects supply with demand
geo.heading: One platform. Three experiences.
geo.lead: P2L connects people, businesses, goods, and services by location. Everything tied together by geographic channels, geofences, and broadcast.
geo.airbnb_text: Discover businesses, properties, products, and services near you. An Airbnb-like reference: local supply appears when you are in the zone.
geo.delivery_title: Request what operates in your area
geo.delivery_text: Restaurants and shops set their radius. Users order products and services through the channel — a Rappi-like reference, inside P2L.
geo.geofence_text: The company activates a broadcast (geofence), publishes its offer, and nearby people subscribe to the channel and chat. When they return to the zone, they can reconnect.

footer.blurb: P2L connects people, businesses, goods, and services by location. Mobility, local marketplace, and deliveries with geographic channels and broadcast.

payments.meta_description: P2L does not collect or hold the value of services. Payment happens between the parties. Platform cost is prepaid from the company balance; it is not charged again on each trip.
payments.title: P2L operating and payment model
payments.lead: P2L connects passengers, operators, and companies without holding trip money.
payments.problem: The issue is not the financial model, but the language. Terms like Settlement, ledger, driverShare, or take rate are technically correct, but they sound like internal accounting to an end user.
payments.names_note: Technical names stay in parentheses when they help development docs. The commercial term comes first.
payments.s1_img_alt: P2L costs, fares, transactions, and payment plans diagram
payments.s1_img_caption: P2L does not charge a commission on the value of each trip. The company contracts and prepays for platform use through a plan and a prepaid balance. The trip value is split between the driver and the company according to the operating conditions defined by the company.
payments.s1_p1: P2L does not receive or hold the money the passenger pays for the trip. The passenger pays the driver directly. The driver settles economically with the company, according to the operation’s rules. P2L only records that split; it does not transfer those amounts.
payments.s1_p2: The company buys a plan. That plan covers the platform cost: no extra percentage is charged at trip time.
payments.quote: P2L does not collect or hold the value of services performed between users, companies, and operators. Payment is made directly between the parties. P2L’s cost is paid in advance through the company balance. On each trip, P2L records and consumes the corresponding amount from that balance, but it does not receive money again from the passenger or the operator.
payments.s1_p3: P2L’s cost is a prepaid technology operating cost, not a commission charged again on each trip.
payments.s1_p4: These two sentences explain almost the entire financial model in plain language.
payments.split_driver_text: Trip share. Receives the passenger payment
payments.split_p2l_text: The plan covers the platform cost
payments.pax_l1: Sees the estimated value before requesting.
payments.pax_l2: Can join a bid when that option is enabled.
payments.pax_l4: Does not pay P2L for the trip. P2L does not receive that money.
payments.op_l1: Completes the trip and receives the passenger payment directly.
payments.op_l2: Records the final value and payment method in P2L.
payments.op_l3: Settles the company share economically (in the example, $4,000). P2L does not transfer that money.
payments.op_l4: Does not need a personal P2L balance. P2L does not charge the driver again for the trip.
payments.co_l2: Sets fares within the limits defined by P2L.
payments.co_l3: Buys a plan or tops up a P2L balance to use the infrastructure.
payments.co_l4: Reviews trips, shares, and prepaid-balance consumption.
payments.co_l5: The $4,000 in the example is the suggested company participation / gross income from the trip.
payments.pl_l1: Provides the technology that connects passengers, operators, and companies.
payments.pl_l2: Records trips and the economic split (80 / 20 / 0).
payments.pl_l3: The plan covers the platform cost. It does not charge an extra percentage at trip time.
payments.pl_l4: It does not charge the passenger or the operator again on each trip.
payments.pl_l5: Does not hold or settle trip money between the parties.
payments.vocab_note: The accounting term accrual is avoided in user-facing docs. Use 20% company participation / gross income instead.
payments.s4_p1: P2L is covered by the company plan and prepaid balance. There is no commission on the trip value.
payments.s4_name: P2L service covered by the plan and prepaid balance
payments.s4_p2: The passenger pays the operator directly. The company defines or receives a share of the trip value. P2L already monetizes its service through the plan and the company’s prepaid balance: it does not charge again at trip time.
payments.s4_ledger_lead: There are two accounting flows in parallel. One is plan consumption by the registered company. The other is the passenger payment to the driver, which P2L only records.
payments.s4_ledger_img_alt: Two accounting flows: plan consumption and trip payment
payments.s4_ledger_img_caption: P2L does not calculate a commission on the trip value. It monetizes with the plan and prepaid balance. Passenger money goes to the driver; the company receives its share outside P2L.
payments.s4_plan_text: The registered company pays the plan. That payment funds the balance. P2L consumes platform use from that balance.
payments.s4_ride_text: The passenger pays the driver. P2L records the trip and the split with the company (80 / 20 / 0). It does not transfer that money.
payments.s4_ledger_company: The registered company does not collect the trip through P2L. It receives its 20% from the driver, according to the operation’s rules. The plan enables the infrastructure; the trip is settled between the parties.
payments.s5_p1: The company defines or receives that share of the trip value. The passenger pays the operator. P2L does not present that percentage as an extra charge at trip time: its service is already covered by the plan and the prepaid balance.
payments.s6_p1: The plan covers the platform cost (0% on the trip). The company receives 20% of the value: $4,000. P2L does not charge the passenger or the operator again.
payments.s6_p2: The passenger hands $20,000 directly to the driver. P2L does not receive that $20,000.
payments.s6_l2: The driver does not physically receive $16,000.
payments.s6_p3: The $16,000 / $4,000 / $0 figures are the recorded economic split. P2L does not make three transfers. The driver settles with the company. P2L only records that $4,000 is the company share. The plan covers the platform cost.
payments.s6_p4: The plan covers the platform cost. On this trip that cost is 0% of the amount the passenger pays.
payments.s6_p5: The $4,000 is the suggested company participation / gross income from that trip. It is not a return on investment.
payments.s6_key: The plan covers P2L’s cost. On each trip P2L does not charge an extra percentage to the passenger or the operator.
payments.s6_r4: P2L platform usage (the plan covers the cost)
payments.s6_r7: P2L deducts from the prepaid balance
payments.s6_clarify_lead: P2L does not receive the $20,000 and does not resolve inside its platform:
payments.s6_c5: bank reconciliation of each passenger payment
payments.s7_p1: For an end user, wallet can sound like P2L holds passenger money. The commercial name is company P2L balance.
payments.s7_p2: The P2L balance is a prepaid amount the company uses for infrastructure. It is not passenger money and it is not the drivers’ balance. The plan covers the platform cost: in the example trip that cost is $0.
payments.s7_flow: Company → tops up P2L balance → P2L consumes platform cost from the balance → the company can keep operating.
payments.s8_l1: The passenger pays the driver directly.
payments.s8_l2: The driver records the final trip value.
payments.s8_l3: P2L records the split: operator, company, and prepaid platform cost.
payments.s8_l4: The driver settles the company’s share. P2L does not transfer that money.
payments.s8_l5: P2L consumes the trip’s platform cost from the prepaid balance. It does not charge the passenger or the operator again.
payments.s8_l6: The company tops up its balance when needed.
payments.tech_p1: Internally, plan consumption is stored in subscriptionpayments, companywallet, and wallettransactions. The trip and its split (80 / 20 / 0) are stored in rides and ridesettlements. There is no commission calculated on the trip value.
payments.tech_p2: There are two language layers: the top layer is clear to any business owner or user; the bottom layer is for the developer reading the system docs.
payments.cta_text: Top up your balance and operate with a clear split: 80% operator, 20% company, 0% platform (the plan covers the cost).
